title: A 4.69mW LLM Processor with Binary/Ternary Weights for Billion-Parameter Llama Model
problem: Running billion-parameter LLMs on edge devices requires extreme power efficiency; standard precision weights consume orders of magnitude more power than practical for mobile/IoT.
motivation: On-device LLM inference enables privacy, low-latency response, and reduced cloud costs, but power consumption is the primary bottleneck.
method: The processor reduces each neural network weight from 32 bits down to just 1-2 bits—this extreme quantization lets you store many more weights in the same memory. It then runs calculations on these tiny numbers using specialized hardware circuits designed for speed and efficiency. When quantized weights become zero, the custom dataflow automatically skips them, avoiding wasted memory access and computation.
key_novelty: Running billion-parameter Llama models using 4.69 milliwatts by shrinking weights to 1-2 bits and using hardware built specifically for calculations on these tiny numbers.
contributions: Hardware design achieving 4.69mW for billion-parameter LLM inference
Binary/ternary weight quantization methodology maintaining model accuracy
Specialized compute pipeline for 1-2 bit arithmetic
Energy-efficient SRAM-based weight storage avoiding DRAM
limitations: Accuracy impact of extreme quantization and comparison with other edge LLM processors not detailed.
primary_theme: Ultra-low-power LLM inference via extreme quantization
